title: model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen GQA/MQA tuning and KV cache scheduling
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: observed model-specific performance regressions and jitter for Llama, Mistral and Qwen families under mixed workload patterns; earlier generic optimizations left pathological cases for GQA- and MQA-quantized variants. This PR contains a set of targeted runtime changes to kernels, scheduler heuristics, KV-cache layout and continuous-batching thresholds to improve p50/p95 latency and throughput consistency for these models, while keeping fallbacks conservative. Summary of changes: 1) Llama attention kernel: introduced a fused rotary+attention kernel path that avoids an extra copy for 4-bit MQA layouts and improves memory access for grouped-quantization (GQA) by aligning per-head blocks; added a microkernel switch to use the fused path when sequence length <= 1024 and batch_size <= 8 to reduce launch overhead; 2) Mistral quirks: adjusted rotary embedding decode to support odd hidden-dim alignments introduced by Mistral 7B variants and added a fast-path for early-termination tokens to reduce KV reads; 3) Qwen KV-cache layout: implemented a compacted KV storage format for the Qwen family that reduces memory pressure for long context use cases and added a small in-place compaction routine triggered when live_kv_ratio drops below 0.6; 4) GQA/MQA tuning: algorithmic heuristics for per-layer kernel choice were extended to recognize GQA/MQA patterns and prefer int4-optimized matmul kernels with corrected scaling factors to avoid small numeric regressions; 5) Scheduler and continuous batching: updated the runtime scheduler to include hot-model affinity (route repeated short requests to warm worker queues), reduced batching window for low-latency classes, added a soft-preempt to flush tiny batches after a 1.2ms idle threshold to avoid tail amplification; 6) KV-cache prefetch + eviction: introduced proactive KV prefetch for predictable next-token patterns and an eviction heuristic that compacts KV slices for shardable workers to improve cache locality; 7) Tests and benchmarks: added model-specific microbenchmarks and end-to-end canary suites for Llama-2-7B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen-2-7B under mixed short/long sequence workloads. Performance: internal benchmark vs main as of 2026-02-28 shows Llama-2-7B int4 GQA throughput +18% p50 latency -12% p95 latency -9%; Mistral-7B early-termination workloads p50 -20% p95 -15%; Qwen-2-7B long-context throughput +25% memory use down 14% in critical scenarios. CI: unit tests and integration canary passed except an initial flaky KVMock test that was addressed in follow-up commit. Backwards compatibility: default runtime behavior unchanged unless model-specific flags detected, feature gated behind `runtime.model_tuning.v1` for safe rollout. Checklist: [x] kernel changes covered by unit tests [x] microbench harness added [x] canary results attached [x] release notes drafted [x] feature flagged for rollout Related work: ENG-4123 (scheduler improvements), ENG-4277 (kv-cache compaction), ENG-4332 (int4 kernel registry).

Improves throughput and p95/p99 stability for mixed short/long workloads. Feature gated behind runtime.model_tuning.v1.
